title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 19-20
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 19 to 20 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'महाबुद्धिर्महावीर्यो महाशक्तिर्महाद्युतिः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 19 to 20 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 19 to 20.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 19 to 20** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **महाबुद्धिर्महावीर्यो महाशक्तिर्महाद्युतिः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**महाबुद्धिर्महावीर्यो महाशक्तिर्महाद्युतिः । अनिर्देश्यवपुः श्रीमानमेयात्मा महाद्रिधृक् ॥** **महेष्वासो महीभर्ता श्रीनिवासः सतां गतिः । अनिरुद्धः सुरानन्दो गोविन्दो गोविदां पतिः ॥**

Great wisdom, great valour, great power and great radiance are his. Of a form beyond description, glorious and immeasurable is that God of gods. He lifted the great mountain. He bears the great bow and carries the earth. The one on whose chest Lakshmi dwells, the refuge of the good, is that God of gods. Aniruddha, the joy of the gods, Govinda, lord of cows and of the wise.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 19 to 20 mean?
faq.a: Great wisdom, great valour, great power and great radiance are his. Of a form beyond description, glorious and immeasurable is that God of gods. He lifted the great mountain. He bears the great bow and carries the earth. The one on whose chest Lakshmi dwells, the refuge of the good, is that God of gods. Aniruddha, the joy of the gods, Govinda, lord of cows and of the wise.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
